status: post_readback_metric localization test fixed before endpoint
question: Does species-specific prior strong-chorus memory decay continuously with geographic distance from the nearest previously strong chorus site?
population: Physically stable matched pairs with at least one prior eligible run in the same State x RouteNumber x RunNumber stratum. Focal species are route-new in the wet survey, occurred somewhere on the route before the focal pair, and have at least one prior CallingIndex 2-3 SiteID with pinned coordinates.
unit: pair x focal species x current physical stop

predictor.nearest_prior_strong_km: Great-circle distance from current SiteID to the nearest SiteID where the same focal species had CallingIndex 2-3 in an eligible run strictly before the earlier focal-pair year.

nuisance_adjustment: log1p(number of other species with prior CallingIndex 2-3 at the current SiteID)
number of prior eligible runs in which the current SiteID was sampled
primary_design: Within each pair x species, demean wet_strong, log1p(nearest prior strong distance), and nuisance covariates. OLS without intercept; cluster covariance by State x RouteNumber.
secondary: Report predicted within-group change in wet_strong for 0 km vs 5 km and 0 km vs 10 km using the fitted log-distance slope.
minimum_gate: At least 500 informative pair x species groups with >=2 unique nearest-distance values, >=250 routes and >=20 species.
interpretation: A negative distance gradient identifies a metric spatial kernel of species-specific acoustic recurrence.
It remains compatible with persistent local populations or fine-scale habitat matching; no individual movement, occupancy continuity, or biological memory is proven.
